_note_dragon_nest: ⚠️ A `_note` IS ONLY SAFE AT THE TOP LEVEL OF THIS FILE, and that is why this one
lives up here instead of beside the entry it describes. `entity_sfx` reads
`units`/`buildings`/`resources` and looks up a def id inside them -- it never
filters `_`-prefixed keys the way GameDataRegistry._read_json does for the roster
files. A note placed inside the `buildings` block on 2026-09-04 was therefore read
as an ENTRY: `entity_sfx` tried to assign an Array to a Dictionary and aborted
eight assertions, and the def-existence test reported `_note_dragon_nest` as a
building that does not exist. The convention differs per file; this file's is here.
THE DRAGON NEST HAS NO `build` ENTRY, AND THAT ABSENCE IS THE HONEST ONE: nobody
builds it (`buildable: false`, PLAN.md 13.2), so there is no villager hammering to
accompany. Only `complete` and `select` are set, which are the two test_audio_seam
requires of every building.
`complete.universal` RATHER THAN `complete.wonder`, even though a henge is the more
wonder-shaped thing. That cue can only ever fire if something spawns the nest as a
FOUNDATION and finishes it, which MapGen will not do -- so it is a sound that should
never be heard, and a triumphal fanfare going off because of a bug would be a loud
way to be told about it. Neutral is the right sound for an event that means
something has gone wrong.
`select.monastery` BECAUSE THE CORE OF THE NEST IS A SHRINE
(`structures/celts/small_stone_monument.xml`). That one genuinely plays: the nest is
selectable, and it is the only sound a player will ever associate with it.
_note: WHICH SOUND EACH ENTITY MAKES (PLAN.md 7.5, A.7). The companion to
audio.json and a different question from it: audio.json maps a sound ID to
a FILE, this maps an ENTITY to a sound ID. Both are ids on both sides here,
so no filename appears in this file and the asset seam is not widened.
WHY IT IS ITS OWN FILE rather than an `sfx` block inside units.json and
buildings.json. Those two carry long _note blocks that are the real design
record for the roster's stats, and adding a fourth concern to 59 entries
there would bury them. Audio is also the one axis where a whole class of
entity shares an answer -- every mounted unit dies the same way -- so a
separate table can say that once instead of 4 times.
HAND-AUTHORED, unlike audio.json, which tools/stage_audio.py generates.
The choice of WHICH 0 A.D. sound suits a unit is a design decision and it
belongs in a file a person edits.
EVERY FIELD IS OPTIONAL AND ABSENCE MEANS SILENCE. A unit with no
`attack` makes no noise when it swings; that is the right default for the
monk, who has no weapon, and it is also what a not-yet-mapped unit does
rather than falling back to a sword it is not holding. MatchAudio asks for
a field and gets &"" if it is not there, which play_sfx treats as nothing
to do -- there is no case where a missing entry is an error.
FIELDS
units.<id>.voice    `male` | `female` -- which latin voice set answers an
order (PLAN.md 9.2.1: latin only). Absent for animals,
ships and siege engines, which have no voice at all.
units.<id>.death    played where it dies.
units.<id>.trained  played flat, not positional, when one of YOURS appears:
it is a report to the player, not an event on the map.
units.<id>.attack   played on the swing, throttled per weapon in audio.json.
units.<id>.idle     ambient noise a living animal makes. Wildlife only.
buildings.<id>.complete / .select / .build
`build` is the construction loop its builders play, and
it is per BUILDING because a stone keep and a timber
palisade do not sound alike.
buildings.<id>.work the gather loop for a building you HARVEST -- the field.
resources.<id>.work / .select
WHY `work` IS KEYED PER RESOURCE DEF AND NOT PER KIND. AnimationSystem
picks its clip from the resource KIND (four of them: wood, gold, stone,
food) because there are only four work animations baked. Sound is finer
grained for free: `food` covers a berry bush, a fish, a carcass and a wheat
field, and foraging, fishing, butchering and reaping are four different
noises 0 A.D. already has. Keying this off `kind` would have thrown that
away to match a limitation that is the ART's, not the audio's.
